brand.audience: Professionals moving into high-impact work in product, Founder's Office, operations, growth and related business roles, or seeking greater decision-making responsibility.
facts: For people moving into high-impact work
Find, prepare, connect, and perform at the opportunities you deserve. All inside a single ecosystem.
Jobs, training, community, rewards, and more, under a single annual membership plan.

A cohort-based programme that builds judgement, problem solving and decision-making under uncertainty. Capability work inside one simulated company, module by module, then Career Translation turning the work into a portfolio and a plan.
Each decision follows from the last, and every call is marked.
Every score comes with the words that define it, so you can see what a top mark asks for and exactly where yours fell short.
Every mark is shown as it was given, never averaged away, so you can see where you were strong and where you slipped.
Your strongest answers, kept exactly as you wrote them, ready to show in an interview or a portfolio.
Your marked work, collected into a proof-of-skill portfolio you can send with an application.
Personal work with a coach: the portfolio, the rebuilt resume and profile, and your transition plan.
Six to eight hours a week: a live session, a simulation, and the reading. Sessions run in IST and are recorded.
Find the right opportunities and pursue them better, build judgement in Proving Ground, or put the whole system around your career with Membership.

angles.idea: Carousel — Applying for a role you have not held: what can you show?
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: make an unfamiliar career programme tangible through the evidence it produces. Awareness hypothesis: the reader recognises a role-transition evidence gap but may know neither Founder's Find nor simulation-based preparation. Opening/payoff pair: begin with applying for a role without the matching title; deliver a concrete distinction between saying you understand decisions and showing a written decision alongside its assessment standard. Story: establish the target-role situation, explain that the work occurs inside a simulated company, show how linked decisions become written answers and individual marks, then explain their collection into a portfolio and use in Career Translation. Each step adds a new understanding rather than repeating a promise. Supported mechanism: published standards, retained answers, raw marks and a proof-of-skill portfolio. Framework: belief/distinction/example/action, with a documented process rather than a fictional success story. Image relationship: supplied portraits cannot evidence this mechanism; use text-led explanation, not an invented scorecard or uninspected diagram. Comparison: high reader recognition, high worthwhile discovery, high specificity, strong credibility for process only, and strong fit with the brand's connection between capability, proof and pursuit.

evidence: Six to eight hours a week: a live session, a simulation, and the reading. Sessions run in IST and are recorded.
You own real work already. The reps make your decisions faster and easier to defend, which is what the next seat up asks for.

angles.idea: Static — Can this career programme fit beside your current job?
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: help a prospective participant qualify the practical commitment, separate from the carousel's explanation of proof. Awareness hypothesis: the reader is considering career preparation but is unsure whether participation can fit their week. Opening/payoff pair: ask what space the programme needs in an existing working week; answer with the documented six-to-eight-hour commitment, its live-session/simulation/reading components, and the fact that IST sessions are recorded. The static communicates this complete idea without requiring a carousel or turning into a broad checklist. Reader takeaway: decide whether there is realistic room for the work before exploring the programme further. Do not imply recordings eliminate all participation requirements or make the programme fully asynchronous. Supported mechanism: a specified weekly workload and recorded sessions. Framework: objection/answer/demonstration through transparent programme terms. Image relationship: none of the supplied portraits shows the workload or teaching schedule, so text-led treatment is more truthful. Comparison: high recognition for employed buyers, moderate discovery, high specificity, strong factual credibility and good brand fit; less novel than the carousel but a useful complementary decision aid.

evidence: A feed built around your role, seniority and city, and the application, outreach and referral request written from your record. Every role is open free, with 5 Job Assists to start: messages to hiring managers, referral requests or application forms.
Every line is checked against your record. You send it, from your own address.
hooks: Help writing to a hiring manager shouldn't mean inventing a stronger CV.
angles.idea: Alternative — Job-search assistance that drafts from your record, not an invented persona
angles.usefulInsight: Content job: explain what the Intelligent Job Board assists with and what remains under the applicant's control. Awareness hypothesis: an active job seeker may want help with applications but hesitate over impersonal or unsupported outreach. Opening/payoff pair: begin with wanting help writing to a hiring manager without overstating experience; explain that drafts draw from the applicant's record, lines are checked against it and the applicant sends from their own address. Supported mechanism: role/seniority/city-based feed, record-based application and outreach assistance, and user-controlled sending. Framework: feature/practical difference/reader value. Image relationship: the portraits do not show this workflow; no authentic interface image was supplied, so avoid fabricated email screenshots. Comparison: high recognition for active applicants, worthwhile discovery and strong product specificity, but weaker campaign cohesion with Proving Ground and less destination precision because no dedicated Job Board page was supplied. This is a distinct search-execution angle, not another portfolio explanation.

strategy.note: The carousel wins on useful discovery: it explains the specific artefacts a prospective career switcher could produce without claiming employers will reward them. The static wins as a complementary qualification post: it answers a practical buying question rather than paraphrasing the portfolio argument. The third idea is credible but serves a more immediate search need and lacks a supplied dedicated product destination. Overall identity comes from the entry page: Intelligent Job Board for finding and pursuing roles; Proving Ground for decision practice and career preparation; Membership for a year of connected support including a programme seat, search support, mentors and meetups. The supporting Proving Ground page supplies the selected campaign's process and commitment details; its length does not make it the whole business. Destination inspection is limited to the supplied page text, not independent live browsing. Proposed carousel family: sequence, reference ID S006-02, because the argument follows documented work-to-portfolio progression. Proposed static family: conversation, reference ID S005-01, using a brand-authored practical question and answer rather than simulated customer messages. These are structural references only; no reference images were inspected or selected as assets. Reader motivations and awareness remain hypotheses. Geography, attendance requirements beyond the quoted schedule, cohort dates and actual participant outcomes are unknown. Exclude testimonials, customer portraits presented as endorsement, placement claims, before/after results, publication logos, numerical uplift claims and scarcity-led use of the stated selection rate. The delivery-crisis scenario and sample outreach are demonstrations, not customer histories; neither is needed for these selected posts. Captions should add context rather than repeat the full argument. No finished slides, captions or design specifications are being proposed here.
strategy.situation: A professional is considering a move into a role they have not held and needs something more concrete than a claim that they can do the work. Another relevant buying moment is evaluating whether a career programme fits alongside an existing job. Motivation hypotheses: these readers want inspectable evidence of their decisions and enough clarity about the commitment to judge fit before applying.

The delivery-crisis scenario and sample outreach are demonstrations, not customer histories; neither is needed for these selected posts. Captions should add context rather than repeat the full argument. No finished slides, captions or design specifications are being proposed here.
strategy.situation: A professional is considering a move into a role they have not held and needs something more concrete than a claim that they can do the work. Another relevant buying moment is evaluating whether a career programme fits alongside an existing job. Motivation hypotheses: these readers want inspectable evidence of their decisions and enough clarity about the commitment to judge fit before applying.

writerRun.review: early-stage-v1: The posts accurately describe Proving Ground’s documented simulation-based practice, linked decisions, published marking standards, retained answers, portfolio support and weekly commitment. They clearly distinguish practice evidence from employment experience and avoid hiring guarantees, invented testimonials or unsupported outcomes. All CTAs point to the supplied Proving Ground page, which supports both the programme mechanism and scheduling details. The carousel addresses a recognisable role-switching situation and advances from practice to assessment to application material, delivering a useful distinction between claiming capability and showing assessed decisions. The static performs a complementary qualification job: budgeting for the full six-to-eight-hour workload rather than only the live session. The intended readers are career-development buyers, not mistakenly assumed to be founders. Text-led treatments avoid irrelevant portraits or fabricated proof, and the described colours and fonts are grounded in the supplied style evidence.

h3: What is Proving Ground?+
p: A cohort-based programme that builds judgement, problem solving and decision-making under uncertainty. Capability work inside one simulated company, module by module, then Career Translation turning the work into a portfolio and a plan. It includes 6 months of the Intelligent Job Board (Foundation plan).
h3: What does it cost, and how do I pay?+
p: ₹34,999 (list price ₹39,999), with 6 months of the Intelligent Job Board included. You book your seat with a part payment and pay the balance before the cohort starts. A counsellor confirms fit on a call before you pay anything, and there is a 7-day, no-questions-asked refund from booking.
h3: How is it taught?+
p: Real cases from real companies (80+ interactive case studies), short action-framework lessons, framework practice, mentor-led live cases, integrated simulations where each decision follows from the last, and feedback marked against a published standard. p: Six to eight hours a week: a live session, a simulation, and the reading. Sessions run in IST and are recorded.

p: Written decisions are marked against a rubric with five written levels, and the feedback comes back in plain language as a conversation about the call you made. Mentors run the live cases and mark the room. Multiple-choice decisions are scored the same way every time, so two people who make the same call get the same score.
h3: Who is it for?+
p: People with a real capability, judgement or proof gap: switchers moving into product, Founder's Office, operations, growth or finance work, and builders sharpening decisions they already make. It is not for someone who wants a certificate.

Common questions.
What is Proving Ground?+

A cohort-based programme that builds judgement, problem solving and decision-making under uncertainty. Capability work inside one simulated company, module by module, then Career Translation turning the work into a portfolio and a plan. It includes 6 months of the Intelligent Job Board (Foundation plan).
What does it cost, and how do I pay?+

₹34,999 (list price ₹39,999), with 6 months of the Intelligent Job Board included. You book your seat with a part payment and pay the balance before the cohort starts. A counsellor confirms fit on a call before you pay anything, and there is a 7-day, no-questions-asked refund from booking.
How is it taught?+

Real cases from real companies (80+ interactive case studies), short action-framework lessons, framework practice, mentor-led live cases, integrated simulations where each decision follows from the last, and feedback marked against a published standard. Case studies, self-paced lessons, masterclasses and the simulation engine are all live today.
How much time does it take each week?+
Six to eight hours a week: a live session, a simulation, and the reading. Sessions run in IST and are recorded.
Who marks the work?+

Written decisions are marked against a rubric with five written levels, and the feedback comes back in plain language as a conversation about the call you made. Mentors run the live cases and mark the room. Multiple-choice decisions are scored the same way every time, so two people who make the same call get the same score.
Who is it for?+

People with a real capability, judgement or proof gap: switchers moving into product, Founder's Office, operations, growth or finance work, and builders sharpening decisions they already make. It is not for someone who wants a certificate.
What do I leave with?+

blocks.text: Founder's Find is built by operators who have seen both career growth and hiring responsibility. Career compounding, and a careers operating system, are the two ideas underneath everything.
Careers changed. Career infrastructure did not.

A career used to be a ladder inside one company. Now it is a sequence of moves across companies, roles and sometimes whole functions, and every product built to help solves one moment of it and stops. Founder's Find is the layer that stays: the opportunity, the selection, the capability, the proof and the people, connected.
Career compounding, and a careers operating system.
